Score trend · v3 scoring basis (full tree, Drive API)

Three v3-basis runs, flat at 61 — a stable system, not an improving one. Audits before 09-07 used a different, narrower scoring basis and are not plotted here. Target 85 is the "runs unattended and trusted" ceiling; the gap is the standing work below.

1 · What this run did

Measured

  • Full-tree census through the Drive API, cloud-only — the laptop was never in the loop. Batched breadth-first over the whole workspace; archive excluded from the score.
  • Kernel-vs-memory drift check: CLEAR. The operating rules on disk and in the cross-surface memory floor agree in substance.
  • Credential scan across the tree — the first-class security pass.
  • Four-pillar score recomputed from this run's census; every figure traces to an API pull.

Published (create-only, nothing moved or deleted)

  • Private master record written to Drive with the full, unsanitised detail — paths, findings, the reversible archive list.
  • Dated history + scheduler snapshot appended as new files (the audit trail is never overwritten).
  • This scoreboard updated in place at its frozen link, and mirrored verbatim to the public handoff file.
  • No autonomous delete, move, or rename — every cleanup is proposed as a list for a human to action by hand.

6 · Action plan · owner: operator

  1. Revoke and delete the flagged credentials.DO NOW Two are live access tokens; revoke at the provider first, then delete — moving them leaves them live. The durable fix is a real secret store or repo authorisation, not a plaintext file in a synced folder. Paths are in the private record.
  2. Restart the parked synthesis task.THIS MONTH It is the single lever on the 4.9% knowledge-base synthesis floor — the system hoards raw intake and rarely distils it. Fix the failure, cap the batch size, re-enable.
  3. Turn off the upstream "convert uploads to Google Docs" setting, then re-export the 12 stubs.THIS MONTH Each stub is a real document reduced to an unreadable pointer — silent data loss. Detection alone is a treadmill; the setting is the source.
  4. Clear the by-hand hygiene list.WHEN CONVENIENT One root stray, a stale label from the workspace rename, a handful of loose backups, a duplicate output folder. All reversible, all listed in the private record; the audit will not touch files unattended.
  5. Stand up the public-mirror route for this scoreboard.SETUP The sanitised page is built and the handoff file is written each run; the public site updates once the mirror repo and its push routine are authorised.

The one human decision that is the bottleneck

Revoke the two live access tokens. They are the only finding with blast radius outside the workspace, and both have sat in plaintext across audits — one is new this month. Everything else on this board is hygiene the system can propose but not execute, or a tracked label a mounted session will fix. The machine has done its job: it censused, scored, caught the exposure, and published — cloud-only, no laptop, nothing destroyed. What it cannot do is revoke a credential. That part is yours.

Sanitised scoreboard. It carries only the score, per-pillar RAG and deltas, trend, plain counts, guardrail PASS/FAIL, and the credential-scan count + PASS/FAIL. It never carries a secret value or path, a file or folder listing, a person's name, an inbox detail, a private financial figure, or an automation trigger URL — those stay in the private .md record on Drive.
